He played college basketball for the [[Niagara Purple Eagles men's basketball|Niagara Purple Eagles]] and [[Tennessee State Tigers basketball|Tennessee State Tigers]]. ==Early life== McCall was born in [[Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]].{{cite news |title=For Philly native Tahjere McCall, working out for Sixers 'a dream' |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/philadelphia-76ers/philly-native-tahjere-mccall-working-out-sixers-dream |access-date=March 22, 2022 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=June 7, 2017}} His father is a locomotive engineer and his mother rehabilitates [[crack cocaine]] addicts.{{cite web |last1=Rexrode |first1=Joe |title=Tahjere McCall is TSU's free spirit, NCAA Tournament hope |url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/college/2017/01/20/rexrode-tsus-tahjere-mccall-true-original/96844488/ |website=The Tennessean |access-date=November 28, 2023 |date=January 20, 2017}} McCall attended [[Carver High School (Philadelphia, Pennsylvania)|Carver High School]] where he did not play on the basketball team until his junior season.{{cite web |last1=Hunt |first1=Donald |title=Former E&S and Tennessee State star Tahjere McCall works out for the Sixers |url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-nba-tennessee-tahjere-mccall-3c7c8fbfc20d47b0a3f741fdd2a1c19b |website=Associated Press |access-date=November 28, 2023 |date=June 6, 2017}} He was preparing to play [[NCAA Division II]] basketball at [[Holy Family University]] when [[Niagara University]] presented him with a scholarship offer. ==College career== McCall began his [[college basketball]] career with the [[Niagara Purple Eagles men's basketball|Niagara Purple Eagles]]. He served as a starter during his freshman season under head coach [[Joe Mihalich]] in 2012–13.{{cite web |last1=Meiler |first1=Mike |title=NU's McCall receives transfer release |url=https://www.niagara-gazette.com/sports/nus-mccall-receives-transfer-release/article_c80ea36a-0c65-5e90-b405-e6c685540157.html |website=Niagara Gazette |access-date=August 26, 2022 |date=March 26, 2014}} McCall was moved to a bench role for his sophomore season by new head coach [[Chris Casey]]. He chose to transfer from the team at the end of the season and joined the [[Tennessee State Tigers basketball|Tennessee State Tigers]] under head coach [[Dana Ford]].{{cite news |author1=Joe Rexrode |title=A true original |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98169295/a-true-original/ |access-date=March 22, 2022 |work=[[The Tennessean]] |date=January 21, 2017 |pages=C1, C3|via =[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}} Ford discovered him through a recommendation from [[Anthony Mason (basketball)|Anthony Mason]] whose son, [[Antoine Mason|Antoine]], played alongside McCall at Niagara. McCall was selected as the [[Ohio Valley Conference]] (OVC) Defensive Player of the Year and earned All-OVC honors during his two seasons at Tennessee State. ==Professional career== [[File:Josh Magette and Tahjere McCall (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|McCall with the [[College Park Skyhawks]] in 2020]] After going undrafted in [[2017 NBA draft]], McCall joined the [[Brooklyn Nets]] for the [[2017 NBA Summer League]] and would join them for training camp. McCall played two seasons with the Nets [[NBA G League]] affiliate in [[Long Island Nets|Long Island]]. On February 26, 2019, he signed a 10-day contract with the Brooklyn Nets.{{cite web |title="BROOKLYN NETS SIGN TAHJERE MCCALL TO 10-DAY CONTRACT" |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-tahjere-mccall-10-day-contract |website=NBA.com |publisher=NBA |accessdate=February 27, 2019}} McCall re-joined the [[Long Island Nets]] after the conclusion of his 10-day contract with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|title=Tahjere McCall Rejoins Long Island Nets|url=https://longisland.gleague.nba.com/news/tahjere-mccall-rejoins-long-island-nets/|date=March 8, 2019|work=NBA.com|accessdate=March 8, 2019}} On September 20, 2019, McCall signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Tahjere McCall|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-tahjere-mccall|website=NBA.com|accessdate=September 20, 2019|date=September 20, 2019}} On October 18, 2019, the Hawks waived McCall.{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/atlanta-hawks-request-waivers-brooks-derrickson-mccall-and-sibert|title = Atlanta Hawks Request Waivers on Brooks, Derrickson, McCall and Sibert|website = [[NBA.com]]}} He was then added to the roster of the Hawks’ G League affiliate, the [[College Park Skyhawks]].{{cite web |title=College Park Skyhawks Announce Training Camp Roster |url=https://cpskyhawks.gleague.nba.com/news/college-park-skyhawks-announce-training-camp-roster/ |website=NBA.com |accessdate=November 17, 2019 |date=October 29, 2019 |archive-date=November 17, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191117202538/https://cpskyhawks.gleague.nba.com/news/college-park-skyhawks-announce-training-camp-roster/ |url-status=dead }} On December 27, 2019, McCall had 28 points, six rebounds, five assists, three steals and one block in a win against the [[Delaware Blue Coats]].{{cite news |title=Tahjere McCall: Leads scoring charge off bench |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/tahjere-mccall-leads-scoring-charge-off-bench/ |accessdate=June 20, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=December 28, 2019}} McCall had two triple-doubles. He averaged 12.7 points on 46 percent shooting, 4.7 assists, 1.9 steals, and 6.1 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Duffy |first1=Dallin |title=Reviewing the College Park Skyhawks Debut Season |url=https://soaringdownsouth.com/2020/06/10/college-park-skyhawks-debut-season/ |website=Soaring Down South |publisher=FanSided |accessdate=June 21, 2020 |date=June 10, 2020}} On January 11, 2021, McCall was selected by the [[Lakeland Magic]] as the 5th overall pick of the month's [[2021 NBA G League draft (January)|2021 NBA G League draft]]{{cite web |title=NBA G League 2020-21 Draft Results |url=https://gleague.nba.com/nba-g-league-2020-21-draft-order/ |website=NBA G League |access-date=January 12, 2021 |date=January 11, 2021}} and averaged 11.3 points, 7.1 rebounds and 3.1 assists through the season.{{cite news |title=Tahjere McCall joins Orleans |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/tahjere-mccall-joins-orleans/ |newspaper=Sportando |access-date=March 29, 2021 |date=March 29, 2021}} On March 29, 2021, McCall signed with [[Orléans Loiret Basket]] of the French [[LNB Pro A|Jeep Élite]]. On August 6, 2021, McCall signed with the [[Cairns Taipans]] for the [[2021–22 NBL season]].{{cite web |title=Taipans Sign NBA G-League Champion, Tahjere McCall |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/taipans-sign-nba-g-league-champion-tahjere-mccall |website=NBL.com.au |access-date=August 6, 2021 |date=August 6, 2021}}{{cite news |author1=Kane Pitman |title=Not just a great defender: Tahjere McCall on turning the Taipans around |url=https://www.espn.com/nbl/story/_/id/32927562/not-just-great-defender-tahjere-mccall-turning-taipans-around |access-date=March 22, 2022 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=December 23, 2021}} On April 23, 2022, McCall signed with the [[Otago Nuggets]] for the [[2022 New Zealand NBL season]].{{cite web |last=Cheshire |first=Jeff |title=Nuggets announce their third US import |url=https://www.odt.co.nz/sport/basketball/nuggets-announce-their-third-us-import |website=[[Otago Daily Times]] |access-date=April 23, 2022 |date=April 23, 2022}} He left the team in mid June after being invited to an NBA summer training camp.{{cite web |last=Cheshire |first=Jeff |title=Join us in wishing Tahjere all the best as he heads to the US after being invited to a NBA summer training camp |url=https://www.facebook.com/otagonuggetsnbl/posts/pfbid02TPD3JZ7EPSp6LpsxgECGCzM3T5iXyPZyz7bMtPM9zBp5dQmcQM8PpxFtxFbSSJKl |website=facebook.com/otagonuggetsnbl |access-date=June 16, 2022 |date=June 13, 2022}} On May 31, 2022, McCall re-signed with the Taipans on a two-year deal.{{cite web |title=Taipans re-sign Tahjere McCall |url=https://www.taipans.com/news/taipans-re-sign-tahjere-mccall |website=Taipans.com |access-date=May 31, 2022 |date=May 31, 2022}} Following the [[2022–23 NBL season]], he joined [[Fos Provence Basket]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].{{Cite web|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/tahjere-mccall-joins-fos-provence/|title=Tahjere McCall joins Fos Provence|work=Sportando |date=March 19, 2023|language=En|access-date=March 20, 2023}} On December 9, 2023, he had 19 points and 15 assists in a 116–101 win over the [[Adelaide 36ers]].{{cite web |title=Taipans produce late rally to defeat 36ers |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/taipans-produce-late-rally-to-defeat-36ers |website=NBL.com.au |access-date=June 16, 2023 |date=December 9, 2023}} Following the [[2023–24 NBL season]], he joined [[Hapoel Holon B.C.|Hapoel Holon]] in Israel.{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/fiba-champions-league/1634578/tahjere-mccall-signs-with-hapoel-holon-basketball-champions-league/|title=Tahjere McCall moves to Israel for the rest of the season|date=February 25, 2024|website=eurohoops.net|access-date=April 23, 2024}} On November 26, 2024, McCall signed with the [[Guangzhou Loong Lions]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].{{cite web |title=广州龙狮官宣外援麦考尔加盟球队，将身披22号球衣，曾入选NBA G联赛最佳防守阵容 |url=https://www.sohu.com/a/830577874_121019331/ |website=九派新闻 |access-date=December 5, 2024 |date=November 26, 2024}} On February 7, 2025, McCall signed with the [[Lokomotiv Kuban]] of the [[VTB United League]].{{cite web |title=Добро пожаловать, Таджер! |url=https://lokobasket.com/news/308591/ |website=ПБК Локомотив-Кубань |access-date=February 7, 2025 |date=February 7, 2025}} On November 16, 2025, Tahjere signed with [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA).{{Cite web |title=Sina
